question: A book, originally priced at ₹600, is subject to a reduction in cost through two consecutive discounts: an initial markdown of 10%, followed by an additional 20% discount. The question then is to determine the conclusive selling price of the book once both these successive price adjustments have been applied.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Using the successive discount multiplying factor method:

Final SP = MP × (100 − D₁)% × (100 − D₂)%

Final SP = 600 × (90 ÷ 100) × (80 ÷ 100)

Final SP = 600 × 0.9 × 0.8 = 432

**∴ The correct answer is ₹432.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Original Marked Price (MP) = ₹600

First successive discount = 10%

Second successive discount = 20%

**Formula Used:**

Selling Price (SP) = MP − Discount Amount

Discount = Rate% of Base Price

 
 
 ₹600
 Marked Price

 
 
• 
 

 −10%

 
 
 ₹540
 After 1st Disc.

 
 
• 
 

 −20%

 
 
 ₹432
 Final SP

 
 Step-by-Step Discount Reduction

**Calculations:**

⇒ First discount amount = 10% of 600 = (10 ÷ 100) × 600 = ₹60

⇒ Price after first discount = 600 − 60 = ₹540

⇒ Second discount amount = 20% of 540 = (20 ÷ 100) × 540 = ₹108

⇒ Final Selling Price = 540 − 108 = ₹432

**∴ The correct answer is ₹432.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Equivalent Successive Discount

When two successive discounts of a% and b% are given, the single equivalent discount is calculated as: D = a + b − (a × b) ÷ 100.

Marked Price vs Selling Price

Discounts are always evaluated on the Marked Price (MP). Hence, the base value changes after every applied discount, making Selling Price (SP) = MP − Discount.

Fraction Method for Discounts

A 10% discount implies the new price is 90% (or 9/10) of the original, while a 20% discount implies the new price is 80% (or 4/5) of the base value. Multiplying these fractions provides direct and accurate results.
